rules.rule: Check for urgent abnormal thoughts or behaviour conditions
rules.problem: Task check_for omits page red-box items: recent head injury, recent seizure, suicidal thoughts, hypoxia/difficulty breathing (RR>30, SpO2<94), glucose <3 / <4 diabetic / >=11.1, dehydration signs, HIV with positive cryptococcal antigen. These are manage-urgently steps, but several are findings the page asks the clinician to look for. 'Asymmetric' is dropped from the stroke signs. 'Reckless' (mania) not encoded.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible stroke in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: 'asymmetric' qualifier on weakness/numbness dropped (no SNOMED laterality used); page says 'consider stroke or TIA' with identical triggers so stroke and TIA rules are duplicated, acceptable.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible TIA in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Identical condition to stroke rule; page does not distinguish. 'Asymmetric' dropped.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable delirium in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
Diagnose probable mania in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Any single one of four soft findings (talkative->Pressure of speech, irritable) gives probable mania; page lists them as alternatives but 'reckless' is missing and 'talkative' mapped to the stronger 'pressure of speech'.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable psychosis in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
Diagnose probable stimulant drug intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Page box is a list of signs without explicit 'any of'; the rule fires probable stimulant intoxication on a single non-specific sign such as nausea or sweating. Also no stimulant exposure required. Reading is plausible but loose.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable alcohol intoxication in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Any single of four signs gives probable; page lists them in one box without 'and/or' so reading is ambiguous. Acceptable.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable alcohol/drug withdrawal in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: 'Known alcohol/drug user' context not encoded; reduced drug intake not covered (only 'abstinent'); 'sweating, nausea' sensitive signs fire with any stopped-drinking finding.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable poisoning in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
Diagnose possible dementia in abnormal thoughts or behaviour
rules.problem: Page places this under 'not needing urgent attention', but the rule has no exclusion of the urgent priority, so dementia is suggested also in urgent presentations. Dementia criteria themselves (onset >=6 months ago) are correct.

rules.rule: Urgent: abnormal thoughts or behaviour of sudden or recent onset
rules.problem: Structure and level are right (red box -> Urgent). Page 'Refer urgently unless' exceptions (known stable schizophrenia, diabetes low glucose resolving with dextrose, known alcohol use otherwise well) are not encoded, so Urgent fires for those patients.

summary: Individual conditions are largely faithful to the page, with only a few imprecise concept mappings (talkative to Pressure of speech, disorganised to incoherent speech, reduced drug intake). The most consequential gaps are structural: the 'Refer urgently unless' exceptions are not encoded so Urgent always fires, the dementia rule is not restricted to the non-urgent branch, and several red-box checks (head injury, seizure, suicidal thoughts, glucose, hypoxia, cryptococcal antigen) are absent from the check task. Several diagnosis boxes fire on a single non-specific sign, which is a loose reading of the page.
